title: Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis Approximation Based on Performance Counter Architecture for SiFive RISC-V Processors
problem: Modern Out-of-Order RISC-V CPUs have complex microarchitectures making performance analysis challenging, and interpreting Performance Monitoring Unit data requires deep architectural knowledge that is difficult for developers to acquire.
motivation: Enabling software developers to profile and optimize RISC-V workloads effectively without requiring extensive microarchitecture expertise.
method: The approach diagnoses performance problems in RISC-V processors by using predefined formulas to combine measurements from hardware performance counters (sensors that track CPU activity) and classify issues into four categories. It validates this method by running standard benchmark programs (SPEC CPU2006) on SiFive RISC-V processors and checking whether the diagnosed problems match actual hardware behavior.
key_novelty: This is the first adaptation of Intel's Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis methodology (a way to diagnose why processors run slowly) to RISC-V processors, with clearly-defined performance metrics validated through hardware performance counter measurements.
contributions: Designed and implemented TMA for RISC-V CPU architecture with formally defined performance metrics
Developed test cases and validation methods for TMA metrics and PMU implementation verification
Demonstrated practical performance analysis framework enabling developers to profile workloads without deep microarchitecture knowledge

metrics.accuracy: TMA bottleneck classification accuracy against actual performance behavior
metrics.other: Metric alignment with performance counter measurements

limitations: Work addresses only TMA Level 1 implementation; comparison with alternative RISC-V performance analysis methods and scalability to complex workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: RISC-V performance characterization via top-down microarchitecture analysis
